thread:
alex: brew installed redwoodctl on my M1 but `redwoodctl localserve` fails with 'no profile found' and my app can't start. binary is at /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl but `redwoodctl` returns: 'command not found' in zsh. anyone seen this?

maria: can you paste `which redwoodctl` and `redwoodctl --version` and `echo $PATH`?

alex: `which redwoodctl` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl
redwoodctl --version -> redwoodctl 0.29.1
echo $PATH -> /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin

nate: looks like zsh isn't loading /opt/homebrew/bin. on M1 homebrew default prefix is /opt/homebrew — zsh on new macs reads ~/.zprofile, not ~/.zshrc, for login shells. try: `echo 'eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"' >> ~/.zprofile && source ~/.zprofile` or create a symlink: `sudo ln -s /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` if you prefer.

alex: applied the zprofile change and `which redwoodctl` now shows /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl, `redwoodctl localserve` starts but now `redwoodctl login` goes into a browser auth loop — browser opens, I approve, then CLI prints "authorization failed, retrying" repeatedly and eventually `device flow expired`. logs show: `auth: device_code exchange 401 invalid_grant`.

maria: are you using a corporate browser extension or privacy plugin? those sometimes block the redirect. also check `redwoodctl login --device-code` to copy/paste the code instead of relying on the callback.

alex: tried `--device-code`, still 401. i dug into ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json and saw an old profile with a stale access_token and weird expiry timestamps. tried `redwoodctl logout` but it didn't remove the local file.

devex-bot: Known issue: cached profiles can become corrupt after a failed migration; deleting `~/.config/redwood/profiles.json` is a safe recovery step. Workaround documented in internal KB: https://internal.redwood/devex/auth-cache-fix (DX-4821).

jen: filing a tiny install/upgrade follow-up: installer should ensure brew shellenv lines are added to ~/.zprofile for common shells and `redwoodctl logout` should remove corrupt profile files. i'll open an issue and flag the auth team. @devex-bot can you add DX-4821 to the tracker?

devex-bot: DX-4821 added to tracker and assigned to @jen. Suggested PR: detect unreadable profiles.json and fallback to empty profile set at startup.

alex: deleting profiles.json fixed it. `redwoodctl login` completed and localserve is back. thanks everyone.

maria: awesome. for follow-up: can you paste the output of `stat ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json` before you delete next time? adding file-permissions/logging would help debug. also adding a user-friendly error when profile parsing fails would reduce onboarding pain. :thumbsup:

alex: will do and attach if it happens again. thanks!
